title: Contract tactical notes — safety & liability clauses (scratchpad)
body:
Purpose: quick personal scratchpad for clauses I should flag during commercial SaaS negotiations. Not a final playbook — keep terse, action-oriented, and include fallback language.

Top priorities (one-liners):
1) Indemnity — insist on mutual IP indemnity; avoid unilateral customer-friendly indemnities that require full defense costs for model outputs.
   - Redline target: mutual indemnity with carve-outs for gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
   - Fallback: cap on indemnity obligations tied to contract value; require notice + cooperation clauses.
2) Limitation of Liability (LoL) — keep very explicit caps and exclude consequential damages; carve out statutory liabilities (e.g., data protection fines) but push to be proportionate.
   - Our preference: cap = greater of (12 months fees) or (a fixed floor for enterprise deals).
   - Trade: allow higher cap for enterprise deals in exchange for revenue commitment.
3) Data Use & Model Training — never allow vendor to use customer data to train generic models unless opt-in and with strong de-identification + auditability.
   - Ask: explicit prohibition on using customer content for model training or to improve third-party models.
   - Safe language: permit aggregate, non-personally-identifiable telemetry if disclosed and deletable on request.
4) Security & Breach Notification — SLA for notification (72 hours max for confirmed incidents); require post-mortem and remediation timeline.
   - Also push for right to audit for a subset of enterprise; if not possible, insist on third-party attestation (SOC2 type) and on-site audit triggers only under narrow scope.
5) Service Levels & Credits — define measurable SLOs and reasonable credits; avoid unlimited termination rights for minor breaches.
   - SRE note: align tokens per second, latency windows, and availability definitions with platform metrics (we tend to measure per-region).
6) Data Residency & Deletion — get explicit commitments for location of storage, and guaranteed deletion within X days on termination; include certificate of deletion for sensitive customers.
7) Confidentiality & Residuals — limit residuals to short period and narrow scope; be wary of broad "residuals" that permit reverse-engineering based on employee memory.
8) Subprocessors / MSPs — require notice of subprocessors and right to object for regulated customers. Include flowdown obligations.
9) Audit and Compliance — prefer third-party reports; if custom audit requested, limit frequency, scope, and cost allocation.
10) Export Controls & Sanctions — ensure both parties have representations; carveouts for legal compliance operations.

Negotiation talking points (snappy):
- "We can agree to indemnify for IP claims where our delivery copies a third-party component, but not for customer-provided prompts or outputs that reference third-party IP without our involvement."
- "Limiting liability to the fees paid in the last 12 months is a standard market compromise; for strategic deals we can expand with a cap ladder tied to committed spend."
- "On training: we will not use raw customer content to improve models unless there is an explicit opt-in and clear anonymization rules; telemetry for platform health is OK and reversible."

Example redline snippets to paste into edits: (short, clipboard-ready)
- Indemnity (mutual): "Each party shall indemnify, defend and hold harmless the other from third-party claims arising from the indemnifying party's breach of its representations or infringement of third-party intellectual property, except to the extent caused by the other party's gross negligence or willful misconduct."
- Limitation of Liability: "Except for each party's indemnity obligations, gross negligence, or willful misconduct, neither party's aggregate liability arising out of or related to this Agreement shall exceed the greater of (1) the fees paid by Customer to Vendor under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim, or (2) $250,000."
- Training prohibition: "Vendor shall not use Customer Data to train, improve or develop any models or services offered to third parties, except where Customer provides a written opt-in. Customer Data shall be processed solely for the purposes set forth in this Agreement and in accordance with Customer's instructions."

Open questions / flags to resolve during review call:
- How do we handle downstream developer use of model outputs (e.g., customers embedding outputs in public sites)? Do we require indemnity protections?
- For enterprise customers requiring high LoL, what's the minimum revenue threshold to trigger higher caps?
- Data subject request handling: need process map and SLA for deletion/DSR responses. Who owns costs?
- Crypto / confidential computations: if customer asks for HSM/KMS integration, confirm product support and runbook for key rotation and billing implications.

Short checklist for redlines before sending to counterparty:
- [ ] Indemnity: mutual? carve-outs present? defense notice + control?
- [ ] Liability cap: number, exceptions listed?
- [ ] Data training clause: explicit prohibition or opt-in?
- [ ] Breach notice: timebox <=72 hours for confirmed incidents
- [ ] Subprocessor list + flowdowns
- [ ] Data residency + deletion described and timebound
- [ ] Audit: SOC2 attestation attached or audit terms narrow
- [ ] SLA metrics match platform definitions (region, window, availability calc)

Quick negotiation agendas (for 30-minute syncs):
- 0-5m: confirm scope & key customer concerns (IP, privacy, compliance)
- 5-15m: walk through indemnity + LoL + training clause proposals; note hard vs soft positions
- 15-25m: align on SLOs, breach notice, and data deletion timelines
- 25-30m: next steps + owner for redlines; decide on escalation to product/engineering for technical commitments.

Tiny templates for email to counterparty legal (tone: pragmatic, short):
- "Thanks — attached redlines. Our main asks: mutual indemnity, reasonable liability cap (12 months fees), and no training on customer content without written opt-in. Happy to walk these during a 30m call if useful."

Notes to self (todo / followups):
- Check Confluence page on Model Training Policy to confirm exact definition of "Customer Data" (Confluence link above).
- Ask SRE to produce SLA extract for latency and availability metrics to include in exhibit.
- If customer insists on broad audit right, draft narrow sample language limiting to security controls and with cost-sharing.

End of scratchpad. Keep this file as the quick starting point for redlines; when a clause becomes "standard" move to legal templates repo.
